_doc: The execution-profile document, whole. Copy it to
manager/local/profiles.json and edit, or point BOARD_AGENT_PROFILES at
a copy elsewhere. This file is documentation: core never reads it, and
a board with no document at all resolves on BOARD_AGENT_COMMANDS plus
the adapter's built-in git/gh grants — exactly the behaviour bench had
before profiles existed. Writing a document is how you get more; it is
never required.
It is machine-local on purpose. It names roots on THIS disk and
capabilities THIS adapter declares, so it belongs with the tool
(manager/local/ is gitignored) and not in the application's history.
Nothing here is ever committed, pushed or carried into a PR body.
WHAT A PROFILE IS RESOLVED FOR
One per launch intent: `work`, `act-pr`, `review`. An intent the
document says nothing about falls back to the legacy settings, so a
document may configure one intent and leave the others alone.
A PROFILE NARROWS; IT NEVER WIDENS
publication.commit/push/publish may be turned OFF for an intent that
has them and never ON for one that does not — `review` asking for
push is refused by name. The built-in git/gh grants per intent are
the adapter's own knowledge and are not a profile's to change.
WHAT 'commands' IS NOT
It is agent capability, and nothing else. A `manager/local/commands/`
executable is UI registration — a $ chip a person clicks — and being
registered there grants a headless run nothing: resolved profiles
list those separately, every one marked agentCapability: false.
`verify` is a gate requirement, and `prepare` a preparation one:
both are declared, surfaced and recorded, and neither is enforced
yet. They resolve with status `pending` and say so.
HOW STRONGLY ANYTHING IS ENFORCED
A command grant becomes a prefix allow-rule in the adapter's rule
language. That narrows which command lines a run may launch. It is
NOT a sandbox — nothing confines a process already running — and the
resolved profile's `guarantees` block is the single place that says
so. `requires` is how you refuse to run without a real guarantee:
every word in it must be a capability the installed backend declares,
and a profile requiring one nothing enforces is refused rather than
run under a restriction that exists only in the prompt.
THE SETTINGS PRECEDENCE, IN ORDER
BOARD_AGENT_PROFILES > manager/local/profiles.json > the legacy
BOARD_AGENT_COMMANDS and the adapter's built-in grants. A document
that does not parse, or declares a `v` this bench does not read, is a
blocker on every intent — it does not quietly become the old policy.
_doc_shared: Top-level `commands`, `context` and `requires` apply to any intent
that does not name its own. Handy for one brief every run must read.

_doc: An approved readable input. `path` is <root>:<relative path>, with
the root one of worktree, app, work, tool — a word rather than a
path, because the document is read on a machine whose paths are
its own. Resolved, hashed and copied into a read-only bundle
before the model is invoked, so a later edit changes the NEXT run
and not this one.
Refused, fail-closed, every time: a path that is absolute or uses
'..', one that resolves outside its root through a link, a
directory (a directory grant is not a read-only guarantee), a
basename that reads as a credential, and anything over the
512 KiB cap. A required input that is missing or unreadable
refuses the launch by name, with a remedy. `"required": false`
turns that refusal into a note and changes nothing else.
Approval covers these files and nothing beside them. It is not
permission to edit them, to read what sits next to them, or to
publish their contents.
context.name: workflow-brief

_doc: A named command grant. `name` is its identity in the manifest,
the prompt and the UI. `run` is one executable and fixed
arguments — refused if it holds any of ; & | ` $ > < ( ) { }
* ? ! ~ # ' " \ [ ], because a prefix rule cannot see what a
shell would expand those into. The executable must be a bare
name resolved on PATH or an absolute path. `root` is which
approved root it runs in (default worktree).
commands.name: unit-tests

verify._doc: A gate requirement: declared, recorded, not yet enforced.
verify.name: unit-tests
verify.help: a later merge gate will insist this passed

prepare._doc: A preparation requirement: declared, not yet run for you.
prepare.name: migrate
prepare.help: apply this branch's migrations before the run

_doc: The intent the legacy arrangement had no answer for: it got a
hardcoded grant set inside each adapter and nothing else. Here it
is a profile like the others — it runs in the application
checkout, it is granted no project commands unless this names
them, and the only thing it publishes is its verdict.
